buildApp.claimFirst: Claim a publisher id first: the starter is named after it.
buildApp.intro: Publish from a terminal, a script or CI with remoteit-app, the publishing tool. It builds, signs and publishes exactly as New app does — the same manifest, the same packing, the same key file — and it signs on your own machine.
buildApp.key: Use the key file from Create key on the Publisher page. The terminal asks for its passphrase. In CI, set REMOTEIT_APP_KEY_PASSPHRASE as a secret.
buildApp.keyAccess: The tool signs in with an access key from Account, Access keys. It keeps it in ~/.remoteit/credentials, as the Remote.It CLI does.
buildApp.publish: build packs a .tar.gz per platform (linux-arm64=out/arm64/ windows-amd64=out/win/ …) and checks it as Remote.It does. sign signs the manifest with your key.
buildApp.publishRelease: upload puts the files on Remote.It. release gives that release to your devices with the app. The app is private to this account's devices.
buildApp.starter: A web page with a title its owner sets: its manifest, its program and its release notes.
buildApp.title: Build it yourself
buildApp.toolCheck: Its manifest names its version and SHA-256. Remote.It signs it with the same release key as its agent packages.
buildApp.toolNotHere: This server does not have the publishing tool. Ask Remote.It for it.
buildApp.why: In the portal your key is used in a separate, sealed frame that cannot send anything anywhere, but a web page runs the code its site serves at that moment. The tool is code you install once and run on your machine: choose it if you would rather not trust a web page with your key.
